chapter_title: RL Prompt Curation and Replay Data
course_outline_concepts: What an RL-stage 'prompt' is — verifiable or judge-able queries, typically filtered from SFT data
Difficulty mining: rollout-pass-rate filtering, Kimi-K2 / Tülu-3 evidence
Replay buffers in RLHF: when useful, when they bias the policy
Curriculum in prompt space: cold-start prompts vs annealed difficulty
Bridge to synthetic — most 2025 RL prompts are synthetic and Track 3 will generate them

sources.what_to_extract: Why trajectory replay fails in RLHF (IS-ratio explosion across stored tokens, KL-vs-current-ref mismatch); the prompt-level replay pattern that survives (TRL GRPOWithReplayBufferTrainer); variance-weighted prompt sampling; negative-result note from DeepSeek-R1 §3.2 abandoning trajectory replay.

Partial-rollouts replay buffer for 128K-context RL; difficulty mining by pass-rate of 10 SFT samples at high temperature; curriculum sampling and prioritized sampling with weight ∝ (1 − success-rate); length penalty warmup.

Agentic RL prompt pipeline: 20K+ tools, real + simulated environments, outcome-success verifiers filter trajectories; joint RLVR + self-critique rubric reward expands the set of judgeable prompts beyond strictly verifiable ones.

RLVR prompt set construction: only prompts paired with a verifier and a reference answer enter the pool; mixing with RLHF/DPO prompts for breadth; 10M-episode PPO budget; verifiable domains (GSM8K, MATH, IFEval, code).
Formal RLVR setup r(x,y)=v(x,y)∈{0,1}; prompt curation invariant (verifier + reference answer required); three verifier domains; loophole-avoidance discipline; why this collapses the proxy/gold gap.

Historical-variance scoring as a prompt-selection heuristic; one-shot RLVR lifting MATH500 36.0→73.6; evidence that the useful prompts are the high-variance ones, not the many-prompts-average ones; post-saturation generalization.

Distribution-shift derivation: ≈80% of the PPO > offline-DPO gap is on-policy coverage; theoretical grounding for why trajectory replay biases the gradient; iterative DPO closes the gap by re-sampling pairs from current π.
Group-baseline variance math (1/(n-1) for RLOO, similar for GRPO); zero-variance prompts produce zero gradient — links directly to the 'kept prompts' filter.
Coverability framing: a source policy (or buffered rollout) is only useful if its induced distribution covers the target region; foundation for the replay-bias argument from a theoretical angle.
Prolonged RL + reference-policy resets + task diversity expands the reasoning boundary; evidence for curriculum-in-prompt-space; the reset mechanism implicitly re-curates the prompt pool.
